newsitem.title: VIETNAM: Vietnam says still hoping for APEC membership soon.
newsitem.headline: Vietnam says still hoping for APEC membership soon.

text.p: Vietnam said on Friday it still hoped to join the Asia-Pacific Economic Cooperation (APEC) forum soon despite signs that new members will not be let in until 1998 at the earliest.

"...as an Asia-Pacific country and a member of ASEAN, Vietnam's participation in APEC fits the purpose of this organisation and has received support from many countries," a Foreign Ministry spokesman said in a statement.
"We hope it will happen soon," he said.
Southeast Asian countries have expressed strong support for Vietnam's early accession to APEC since it joined the Association of Southeast Asian Nations (ASEAN) last year.

But Philippine Foreign Secretary Domingo Siazon told reporters in Manila on Thursday that although a three-year moratorium on new members will be allowed to lapse at the end of this year, other members will not be brought into the fold immediately.

He said leaders of the 18 APEC members, who will meet in the Philippines on Monday, would announce criteria for new members at their summit in Canada in 1997, and then decide which ones to let in at the following meeting in Kuala Lumpur in 1998.
"It will be a two- to three-year process," Siazon said, adding that new members would attend their first summit in 1999.
The Vietnamese Foreign Ministry spokesman said Hanoi had no information on Siazon's comments.
But Hanoi wanted to underline efforts that the communist country has made to join organisations such as the ASEAN Free Trade Area, APEC and the World Trade Organisation.

"We would like to make clear that during the reform process, Vietnam has made strong efforts and has gained significant achievements in economic reform and policies to integrate into the region and the world," the spokesman said.
ASEAN groups Brunei, Indonesia, Malaysia, the Philippines, Singapore, Thailand and Vietnam.
